entities.name: Cyanuric chloride
observations: Cyanuric chloride is represented as ClC1=NC(Cl)=NC(Cl)=N1 and undergoes amination by nucleophilic aromatic substitution.
A mono-substitution product retains two triazine chlorine atoms.

entities.name: Bicyclic amino ether
observations: The first reactant decodes to C1CC2CNCC1O2, a secondary bicyclic amino ether with an N-H nucleophile.
Its nitrogen is predicted to form the new bond to a cyanuric-chloride triazine carbon.

entities.name: Monoaminated dichlorotriazine
observations: The product is a monoaminated cyanuric chloride derivative with two remaining triazine chlorides; acetone is not incorporated.

entities.name: Cyanuric chloride amination
observations: Base-promoted nucleophilic aromatic substitution replaces one cyanuric-chloride C-Cl bond with the bicyclic secondary amine.
Sodium bicarbonate neutralizes HCl; chloride, water, and acetone are consistent with reaction/workup components.
